edges.description: Loss of EDARADD-mediated NF-κB activation prevents normal induction and morphogenesis of eccrine sweat glands during embryonic development.
Loss of EDARADD-mediated NF-κB activation impairs hair follicle placode induction and morphogenesis.
Loss of EDARADD-mediated NF-κB activation disrupts dental placode signaling and tooth bud morphogenesis, causing hypodontia and conical tooth morphology.
Defective ectodermal appendage development in periorbital skin is associated with characteristic periorbital wrinkling.
Craniofacial ectodermal-mesenchymal developmental alterations in EDARADD-related HED produce mild frontal bossing.
Impaired development of ocular surface exocrine glands (lacrimal and meibomian glands) leads to tear film deficiency and keratoconjunctivitis sicca.
Hypoplasia of respiratory tract submucosal seromucous glands impairs mucociliary clearance and predisposes to recurrent sinus and respiratory infections.
Aplasia or hypoplasia of eccrine sweat glands directly causes reduced or absent sweating.
Inability to sweat leads to impaired evaporative cooling and life-threatening hyperthermia in warm environments or during exertion.
Reduced sweat and sebaceous gland output contributes to generalized skin dryness (xerosis).
Reduced hair follicle numbers and abnormal follicle morphogenesis cause sparse, thin, and slow-growing scalp hair.
Impaired hair follicle development in the supraorbital region causes sparse or absent eyebrows.
Impaired hair follicle development in the eyelid margins causes sparse eyelashes.
Arrested tooth bud development causes congenital absence of multiple deciduous and permanent teeth.
Altered dental cusp patterning during odontogenesis results in conical or peg-shaped crowns.

nodes.description: EDARADD encodes the intracellular death domain adaptor protein—expressed as two alternatively spliced isoforms differing by 10 N-terminal amino acids (205-amino-acid isoform A and 215-amino-acid isoform B)—that self-associates and interacts via its C-terminal death domain with the cytoplasmic death domain of the ectodysplasin A receptor (EDAR), linking ligand-bound EDAR to TRAF6, TAB2, and TAK1 to activate the IKK complex and canonical NF-κB transcription in embryonic surface ectoderm. Biallelic loss-of-function variants (such as c.424G>A [p.Glu142Lys in isoform A / p.Glu152Lys in isoform B], which impairs EDAR interaction while retaining partial NF-κB activity, c.402-407del [p.Thr135-Val136del], or frameshift insertions in the death domain) and heterozygous dominant-negative death domain missense variants (c.335T>G [p.Leu112Arg in isoform A / c.365T>G, p.Leu122Arg in isoform B], c.358G>T [p.Asp120Tyr in isoform B], and c.367G>A [p.Asp123Asn in isoform B], which abolish TRAF6 binding and suppress wild-type EDARADD signaling) abrogate downstream canonical NF-κB activation required for ectodermal placode induction and morphogenesis of eccrine sweat glands, hair follicles, and teeth.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of EDARADD gene mutations responsible for hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we performed detailed in vitro analyses in order to characterize three dominantly inherited missense mutations, p.D120Y, p.L122R, and p.D123N, and one recessively inherited missense mutation, p.E152K, in the EDARADD gene. Nuclear factor (NF)-κB reporter assays demonstrated that all the mutant EDARADD showed reduction in activation of NF-κB. Importantly, p.D120Y-, p.L122R-, and p.D123N-mutant EDARADD slightly reduced the NF-κB activity induced by wild-type EDARADD in a dominant negative manner.
